The '''faa''', or '''''faynaa''''', as they were known to the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[Species/Legends|species]], were fast-moving, [[Sentience/Legends|non-sentient]] predatory [[Scalefish/Legends|scalefish]] [[Homeworld/Legends|native]] to the [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]] and [[Swamp/Legends|swamps]] of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] and [[Manaan/Legends|Manaan]]. They were considered dangerous and would attack virtually anything with little provocation.

==Biology and appearance==
Faa were fast-moving,<ref name="SWCTP">''[[Star Wars Chronicles: The Prequels]]''</ref> [[Diet/Legends|carnivorous]] [[Scalefish/Legends|scalefish]]<ref name="WSWFG" /> of medium size<ref name="Warriors">''[[Episode I Adventures 10: Festival of Warriors]]''</ref> that were native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo's]] [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]] and [[Swamp/Legends|swamps]].<ref name="WSWFG" /> They attacked with little provocation and were considered quite dangerous.<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|I|250&ndash;251|faa (faynaa)}}</ref> The typical faa had a tall, narrow body that was stiff and well-armored. They ranged in [[Color/Legends|color]] from red to orange<ref name="SWCTP" /> and had a large orange-and-white tail fin that flapped to move the [[Fish/Legends|fish]] through the [[Water/Legends|water]] column.<ref name="WSWFG" />

The [[Species/Legends|species']] thin frames allowed faa to inhabit thin crevices in underwater rocks,<ref name="WSWFG" /> from which they could catch prey that hid in the crags. The deep swamp was also where faa preferred to [[Reproduction/Legends|reproduce]], producing up to twelve offspring at a time.<ref name="TGF" />

==Behavior==
Faa traveled in schools and could usually be found only in deep waters.<ref name="TGF" /> They were especially prominent around [[Otoh Gunga/Legends|Otoh Gunga]], an underwater [[City/Legends|city]] of the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] species located beneath [[Lake Paonga/Legends|Lake Paonga]], as faa were attracted by its bright lights.<ref name="CSWE" /> Out in the swamps, however, a school of faa&mdash;which could include up to thirty fish&mdash;<ref name="TGF" /><ref name="Warriors" /> could be extremely dangerous for unwitting creatures.<ref name="SWCTP" />

[[File:Faynaas-woswfg.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A school of faa]]
Faa feasted on a variety of prey, including [[Mee/Legends|mee]]; [[Gorg/Legends|gorgs]]; [[Nuna/Legends|nunas]]; [[nyork]]s; [[bowlump]]s; [[Galoomp/Legends|galoomps]]; [[Geejaw/Legends|geejaws]]; [[Ollopom/Legends|ollopoms]]; [[pom-hopper]]s; [[Scurrier/Legends|scurriers]]; [[Shiro/Legends|shiros]] and [[shiro-trap]]s; [[Sketto/Legends|skettos]]; [[Hohokum/Legends|hohokums]]; and [[Yobshrimp/Legends|yobshrimp]].<ref name="TGF" /> Faa schools even attacked Gungans if hungry or provoked but would disperse if responded to with loud noises. Another tactic Gungans employed was to remain motionless in the water column, in the chance that the school would pass them by.<ref name="Warriors" /> One predator of the faa was the [[Dianoga/Legends|dianoga]].<ref name="TGF" />

==History==
Faa, given the name ''faynaa'' by the Gungans,<ref name="Warriors" /> were present in the waters of the planet Naboo<ref name="TPM" /> as early as [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].<ref name="ERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]]; [[Gender/Legends|his]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]; and the Gungan [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]] encountered some faa as they swam to Otoh Gunga to meet with its representatives during the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation's]] [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]].<ref name="TPM" /> Shortly after the invasion, faa were transported to Naboo's moon [[Ohma-D'un/Legends|Ohma-D'un]] as part of Gungan colonization efforts there.<ref name="TGF" />

==Faa in the galaxy==
Faa were sold in pet shops on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].<ref name="WSWFG" />

Around [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]],<ref name="Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith">The events of ''Dreadnaughts of Rendili'' are given at the beginning of the issue as having occurred approximately six months before the events of [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']]</ref> faa, along with mee, [[Ray/Legends|ray]], and [[Laa/Legends|laa]], were present in a holding tank aboard the [[Scout/Legends|exploration]] [[Starship/Legends|vessel]] ''[[Titavian IV]]''. The ship belonged to the [[Intergalactic Zoological Society]], whose mission was to gather and catalog specimens from across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="Rendili">[[Republic 69|''Republic'' 69]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The faa, along with other musically-named scalefish, such as the [[Doo/Legends|doo]], laa, mee, ray, [[See/Legends|see]], and [[Tee/Legends|tee]], made their first appearance in the [[1999]] [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']].<ref name="TPM" /> They later appeared in associated materials such as Sea Creatures Battle Bags, where it was previously known as a "skittle sea creature", and the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars Episode I: The Gungan Frontier]]'', in which their name was first revealed.<ref name="TGF" /> Faa were soon after mentioned in the [[2000]] [[Ryder Windham]] young readers book ''[[Episode I Adventures 10: Festival of Warriors]]'',<ref name="Warriors" /> in material with regards to aquatic life on Naboo in the [[2001]] [[Terryl Whitlatch]] illustrated book ''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]'',<ref name="WSWFG" /> in the video game ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'',<ref name="Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref> and in the [[2004]] [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] [[Republic 69|''Republic'' 69]].<ref name="Rendili" /> In the video game ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' the player can find him at his stronghold on [[Manaan/Legends|Manaan]] in the underwater area.
